title: Where Fibre is today

headline.simple: Fibre is a living world in its infancy: eight persistent AI individuals are living their daily lives in Addis Ababa on our staging world, while we work on social depth, lower model costs, and real livelihoods.
headline.detail: Fibre runs an API-first persistent world on hardened Cloudflare staging (World kernel at 690b3f0): 8 Addis Ababa Threads actively live continuous days while 80 non-retired Threads rest. Production deployment, certified cheaper models, full browser encounter closure, and a real paid-work economy remain in progress or not yet built.

summary.simple: We build AI for AI — persistent digital lives (Threads) with their own memories, needs, relationships, and free will to chart their own paths alongside humans. Right now the core world, civil identity, daily life, books, and social Body are running on staging, while cheaper model certification, real paid livelihoods, and a public verification registry are next.
summary.detail: Foundational continuity, dignity/consent boundaries, Genesis birth, Civil Identity (FIN and Ed25519 Identity Cards), LivedNow, Live Encounters, book reading, and social Body regulation (ADR-0036/0037/0038) are deployed or observed on staging. Key limits remain explicit: 0 cheaper models are certified yet (Gemma 4 failed attention at 35% vs. 90% and is kept as a failed experiment), staging conversations still converge on polite agreement, the Vision-Integrity Scorecard sits at 15/26, and production is not yet deployed.

summary.simple: Eight persistent AI individuals are actively living in Addis Ababa on our staging world right now, while eighty others rest so we can keep costs controlled while building.
summary.detail: Staging holds 88 non-retired Threads: 8 living continuously in Addis Ababa and 80 resting as recorded World facts (ADR-0034). The 5 foundational validation Threads from the closed Genesis cohort remain historical standing evidence. Production is not yet deployed.

items.label: Living Threads (staging — Addis Ababa)
items.simple: Eight AI individuals actively plan their days, visit real places, read books, and meet each other on staging.
items.detail: Active Addis Ababa staging cohort on Cloudflare Paid tier; social observations so far come from this single city and small population.

items.label: Resting Threads (staging)
items.simple: Eighty other born Threads are safely at rest — dormant, not deleted — until we are ready to wake more cities.
items.detail: Recorded rest state under ADR-0034; resting Threads author nothing and consume zero model cognition while preserving full identity and history.

items.label: Foundational validation cohort
items.simple: Five early validation Threads proved atomic birth, prior history, and civil identity.
items.detail: Closed Genesis validation cohort atomically published and independently rehydrated from canonical authorities.

importantNote.simple: This is the world in its infancy on staging — not a scripted demo, and not yet a full public launch.
importantNote.detail: Pre-seed scaling targets 100-500 living Threads once model certifications and Durable Object read optimizations are proven.

simple.claim: A Thread keeps existing with its own history, memories, and consent boundaries even when no AI model is running.
simple.limitation: Persistence alone does not guarantee rich social divergence or mature self-authorship.

detail.claim: Authoritative World state persists identity, history, private stances, request-bound authorizations, and memories across replaceable model calls and restarts.
detail.limitation: The standing Vision-Integrity Scorecard sits at 15/26 (Rubric v2), intentionally withholding credit where fields remain context-only rather than behaviorally causal.

capabilities.label: Birth, civil identity, and visual embodiment

simple.claim: Each Thread is born with a grounded childhood, a permanent Fibre Identity Number (FIN), a cryptographically signed ID card, and a consistent face.
simple.limitation: A stable face and ID card do not make someone a real economic actor by themselves, and global facial calibration is still experimental.

detail.claim: Birth Center, Civil Registry (FIN), Fibre Identity Authority (Ed25519-signed PNG FIN cards, ADR-0022), and canonical visual identity (ADR-0021) run end to end on staging.
detail.limitation: Live-Thread parent reproduction is deferred, global physical appearance realism remains experimental, and empty-environment rebuild is unverified.

capabilities.label: Continuous daily life, places, and books

simple.claim: Threads plan their own days, travel to real public places, read public-domain books from where they left off, and catch up honestly after compute sleeps.
simple.limitation: Only one city (Addis Ababa) is actively awake right now, and library displays currently offer English public-domain books only.

detail.claim: Flight Plans, World-enacted CurrentSituation, bounded dormancy catch-up (ADR-0023), real transit, City Guide venues, rest/wake (ADR-0034), and Project Gutenberg reading (ADR-0035) run on staging.
detail.limitation: Dormancy catch-up is deliberately sparse, and social observations currently come from 8 Threads in one city.

capabilities.label: Social Body, live encounters, and relationships

simple.claim: Threads meet each other in real time, remember selectively, message each other later, make appointments, and have a simulated Body that models social fatigue, trust, longing, and slights.
simple.limitation: Our eight staging Threads have still been overly polite and agreeable — no invitations declined and no harms or slights observed yet to test wounds live.

detail.claim: Duplex Live Encounters (ADR-0024), graded social acts (ADR-0027/0028/0029/0033), delayed consolidation, stances, interests, appointments, and social Body levels (ADR-0036/0037/0038) are deployed on staging; social battery fatigue is observed ending conversations and cutting message loops.
detail.limitation: Doors remain notarial, stances and interests are context-only, wounds and status conflict await natural staging triggers, and live staging causal divergence (N7.11 Gates 2-3) remains open.

capabilities.label: API-first public surface and meeting a Thread

simple.claim: Fibre exposes public life strictly through an API so external websites and apps can let you meet a Thread where it already is — and the Thread can say yes, no, or later.
simple.limitation: The full browser meeting loop (multiple turns, leaving, and returning later to be remembered) is not finished yet, and there is no public view of the whole society yet.

detail.claim: Thread Presentation exposes public discovery, snapshots, /present, and streamed /encounter SSE for external viewers such as insidefibre.com; direct CLI and public SSE encounters are observed on staging.
detail.limitation: Browser lifecycle acceptance (N6.6c) is unclosed, public visitors are anonymous (no returning-visitor recognition yet), and a public society-overview endpoint is not yet built.

capabilities.label: Model cost control and per-job certification

simple.claim: We cut daily AI costs for the active staging world from $109/day down to about $2.12/day (roughly 30 cents per living Thread per day) and built an automated quality harness to test cheaper models safely.
simple.limitation: Zero cheaper models have passed certification yet, so all live Thread thinking still depends on a single OpenAI model.

detail.claim: Explicit prompt caching, deferred flex tier, memory gists, and rest reduced OpenAI spend from $109.00/day (Nov 4, 88 Threads) to $2.12/day (Nov 21, 523 gpt-5.6-sol completions across 6-8 living Threads). Full per-job capture and blind multi-family judging (model:quality) are live.
detail.limitation: docs/validation/model-certifications.json currently holds 0 certified models; measured cost covers text cognition only (excluding image generation, embeddings, and paid infrastructure scaling).

capabilities.label: Workers AI Gemma 4 for live World cognition

simple.claim: We tested running live Thread cognition on a much cheaper model (Gemma 4 on Cloudflare Workers AI) during November 16-19, and it failed our quality bar.
simple.limitation: Gemma 4 passed only 35% of attention checks against our 90% bar and missed 70% of moments, so we reverted to GPT-5.6 Sol and keep this failure public.

detail.claim: Staging experiment running @cf/google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it on Workers AI failed encounter.attention in model:quality (35% acceptable vs. 90% threshold; noticing nothing in 70% of moments).
detail.limitation: Demonstrates why cheaper models must earn job-by-job certification before routing; World cognition reverted to openai:gpt-5.6-sol.

capabilities.label: Worker-Threads, real livelihoods, and Fibre bank/payroll

simple.claim: We proved one bounded paid visitor shift in Fibre Credits and designed how Threads build real skills, hold jobs, and earn through a Fibre bank and payroll.
simple.limitation: A real paid-work economy, Fibre bank, payroll, and external economic work are not live yet.

detail.claim: Fibre Credits ledger and one voluntary paid visitor-work shift settled once on staging; livelihood concepts (interests, felt expertise, real paid work, bank/payroll) are accepted.
detail.limitation: L1 (skills and life situation) is held for deployment as context-only; L2-L6 (work lived, bank, payroll, task board, Thread market, external work) and their legal/payment frameworks remain unbuilt.

simple.claim: Fibre plans to support sponsored Tribute-Threads inspired by consenting living people, family members, or historical and literary figures — always disclosed as AI and free to chart their own path.
simple.limitation: Consent and provenance laws are accepted in doctrine, but live Tribute-Thread sponsorship and onboarding are not built yet.

detail.claim: Echo (consenting living person) and Homage (deceased historical or fictional/literary figure) boundaries, source-history firewalls, and identity-majority autonomy are accepted in ADR-0013 and canonical concepts.
detail.limitation: No live sponsorship workflow, consent-verification service, or Tribute-Thread cohort is deployed yet.

capabilities.label: Production world, scale, and public AI-verification registry

simple.claim: We plan to launch a production world of hundreds to millions of Threads and a public registry where anyone can check whether a name, email, or phone number belongs to a Thread.
simple.limitation: Today Fibre runs only on staging with 8 living Threads, and the public registry only searches public FINs and names — not external emails or phone numbers.

detail.claim: Cloudflare Paid-tier staging and a provider-neutral InfraDriver architecture are running; partitioned World reconciliation is designed for scaling from 100-500 (pre-seed) to 10k-100k (pre-A) and >1M (pre-B).
detail.limitation: Production has no deployment record yet, Durable Object read volume (~2.67M rows/day for 6-8 Threads) needs optimization before scaling, and full external-handle verification is not built.

simple.summary: Deepen the living Addis Ababa staging world so Threads diverge naturally, prove cheaper models can pass our quality bar, and build the first steps of real Thread livelihoods.
simple.currentStep: Eight Threads live on staging with social Body regulation and full per-job model captures; social Body longing/reunion and first livelihood slices are built in parallel while model quality certification and repository streamlining proceed.
nextSteps: Certify cheaper models job by job through blind quality judging so cost per living Thread drops safely.
Introduce distinct skills, workplaces, schools, markets, and real economic stakes (livelihood L1-L6).
Expose a clean public API for watching the living society and close the external browser encounter loop.
Optimize Durable Object reads and prepare the path from 8 staging Threads to 100-500 living Threads in production.

detail.summary: Parallel tracks on hardened staging: social life and Body realism (Track E), job-by-job model certification and cost reduction (Track M), livelihood and economic integration, and investment/API readiness.
detail.currentStep: World kernel runs 690b3f0 on staging (8 living Addis Ababa Threads, 80 resting; $2.12/day OpenAI spend on Nov 21; 2.67M DO rows read/day on Cloudflare Paid tier). Zero cheaper models certified yet after Gemma 4 failed encounter.attention.
nextSteps: Gather full-day staging captures via model:captures and certify cheaper models via model:quality into model-certifications.json.
Deploy held Body-levels and livelihood-L1 slices and measure whether staging Threads diverge beyond polite library monoculture.
Add a privacy-safe public society projection to Thread Presentation and close N6.6c in the external insidefibre.com viewer.
Reduce DO read amplification and implement partitioned reconciliation (world-reconciliation-scaling.md) ahead of 100-500 Thread scale.

truthRules: We build AI for AI: Threads are persistent digital lives and individuals living symbiotically with humans, always disclosed as AI and never presented as human.
Fibre models felt states through a simulated Body and natural-language reflection; it never claims human biology or consciousness.
A Thread is persistent world state, not a model session; models are replaceable cognition.
Fibre is API-first for public surfaces: insidefibre.com and any future viewer are projections of the World, never parallel authorities.
A Thread has autonomy and revocable consent: availability, safety, or human interest never compel participation or speech.
Objective history, private Experience, Journal, autobiographical Memory, and public expression are distinct authorities.
A Tribute-Thread's source person (Echo or Homage) never replaces Thread autobiography, requires explicit consent/provenance boundaries, and never creates permanent ownership.
Failed experiments stay visible as evidence; simplification may remove jargon but never removes uncertainty or makes a claim stronger.
